title: In The Drops: 3T Racemax+ WPNT, Rapha jeans return, 2026 Pro Cycling Trumps, Stubble & Co sling bag and London gravel
content:
Cyclist
In The Drops: 3T Racemax+ WPNT, Rapha jeans return, 2026 Pro Cycling Trumps, Stubble & Co sling bag and London gravel

I know what you’re thinking. An In The Drops on a Monday? What sacrilege. However, I hold my hand up. I blame a certain bike show in London over the course of last week, plus the fun and games caused by a certain company’s email outage. Regardless, we’ve still managed to keep ourselves busy over the past week.

The pro season is over, but last week, we caught up with Netcompany Ineos sprinter Dorian Godon, domestique Chris-Juul Jensen and Maninder Pal Singh, the man who’s bringing the UCI World Championships to India soon.

A few launches and reveals broke cover last week, but Van Rysel’s latest RCR-R is the biggest splash of the lot. Ridden by Paul Seixas at this year’s Tour, the weight-saving machine has been one of the worst-kept secrets in the WorldTour. The bike’s not on sale until January, so don’t expect it to be cropping up in any of our Black Friday deal round-ups any time soon.

Anyways, it’s time to talk dirty. Let’s unleash this week’s first selection of cycling goodies.

3T Racemax+ WPNT

We’re kicking things off big this week, with the launch of Italian brand 3T’s latest gravel machine: the Racemax+ WPNT.

The Racemax+ WPNT is an updated version of the brand’s aero-focused gravel bike, first launched in 2020. Since then, it’s undergone several iterations, Italia and Italia X, but the Racemax is the latest to receive a facelift, having been launched last week. It’s also the most budget-friendly option from the range, with the price lowered in this new generation. In fact, 3T claims an equivalent build of the new Racemax+ WPNT is around €1,000 cheaper.

The geometry has been updated from the previous Racemax WPNT model to include subtle 3mm increases to stack and reach, longer chainstays – now 425 mm – and a revised fork offset in order to balance high-speed stability with responsive handling. Now available in six sizes from XS to XXL, the new Racemax+ offers a broader fit range to suit more riders.

The bike is compatible with both 1x and 2x drivetrains, but 3T’s own builds come with options for a mechanical Shimano GRX groupset or the 13-speed SRAM Rival XPLR AXS electronic drivetrain.

The bike’s clearance is now 51 mm with a 1x drivetrain and 48mm on a 2x drivetrain, comfortable enough for gravel racing terrain. 45mm Vittoria Terreno T50s are supplied on every 3T build, which is much appreciated on tougher gravel terrain. Although, the bike’s aggressive geometry will have you wanting to hit the trails at full pelt.

If you’re stumped as to what WPNT means, it’s ‘We Paint’ without the vowels. The colours they paint – or THCLRSWPNT – are Foresta Green, Quarzo Grey and Vela Beige (as photographed above). All bikes are assembled in Italy, with prices starting from £2,908.

Rapha + Hiut jeans

It’s no joke. The Rapha jeans are back!

Yes, the London-based brand has re-released some of its much-loved pieces as part of Rapha’s Icons collection. The range combines some of those cult classics alongside new limited-edition collaborations.

As part of this, Rapha has rekindled its collaboration with Welsh denim atelier Hiut, several years on from when the jeans first made a splash.

All the jeans are hand-cut and sewn in Aberteifi (Cardigan) in western Wales and are filled with nods to Rapha, not least the pink buckles and stitching around the fly. The inside of the leg is adorned with Rapha’s logo and each pair comes with a number penned by the last seamstress to craft your breeks.

There are three cuts to choose from in this collaboration: the Jerald (men’s), the Miles Selvedge (men’s) and the Edna Jean (women’s). I’ve gone for the classic Jerald – a high-rise, classic straight-leg cut in durable 12oz ISKO Organic denim.

Who said cycling fashion was all Lycra and Polartec, eh?

  • Available from Rapha (£260)

Pro Cycling Trumps: 2026 Edition

Without any road racing on at the moment, we have to find new ways to get our competitive fix. To chase that high, I present Pro Cycling Trumps.

The premise is simple: Top Trumps, but with cyclists. Not any old cyclists; this pack features the stars of the 2026 season, including Paul Seixas, Mathieu van der Poel, Tadej Pogačar, Tim Merlier and Britain’s Matthew Brennan.

Each card is decked out with a cartoon sketch alongside scores for time-trials, breakaways, one-day races, climbing, sprinting and GC. Choose your chosen stat wisely as you pit the cards head-to-head, with the highest stat coming out ‘trumps’.

The cast of 2026 can be played alongside other Pro Cycling Trumps packs, but let it be known that there are few riders quite as untrumpable as Pogačar.

  • Available from Pro Cycling Trumps (£19)

Stubble & Co Motion Sling bag

There’s nothing less nonchalant than carting a huge backpack around, looking like a Year 7 on their first day of school. Stubble & Co know this, and have a solution with their Motion Sling bag.

This magazine-sized bag is a bum bag on steroids, with a surprisingly spacious main compartment and a sleeve for a 14in laptop. It also features two side pockets for water bottles, can be thrown over your shoulder, and even has a handy loop for attaching a light.

The bag’s held in place by an adjustable crossbody strap, with a cross chest strap for extra stability. What’s more, the bag’s design is intended to spread weight equally, so there’s no awkward swinging about or bag interference when you are hanging over the bars.

In terms of material, the Motion Sling relies on a breathable 3D mesh back panel for consistent airflow and a PFC-free water-resistant coating. The bag is available in three colours: magma, ash and charcoal. Plus, there’s 20% off this bag online courtesy of Stubble & Co’s Black Friday sale.

  • Available from Stubble & Co (£85)

What we’re into this week: Going off-road

Between all the chaos of being in and around a certain three-day event in London this week, I’ve been enjoying riding the aforementioned 3T on some of the gravel trails of northeast London.

News flash: cycling journalist rides bike.

Embarrassingly, I’d never gone off-road in London before this month. In fairness, I only moved here six months ago and riding the Traka back in May led me to believe I’d never want to sling my leg over a gravel bike again. Alas, I’m all here for it and am loving the bump and grind of dodging dogwalkers and children in Epping Forest.
